speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked	 the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the current breakdown of Employment Pass, S Pass and Work Permit holders and the resident workforce in the tech and IT sector; and (b) what are the efforts to ensure that foreign manpower is not over-represented in this sector and the efforts to promote more locals to join the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: More details will be released during the Ministry of Communication and Information (MCI)'s Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I am also very encouraged that the Ministry for Manpower (MOM) has consistently gone after the "double weak" companies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister if he has observed any "double weak" companies in the ICT sector and what are the actions against these "double weak" companies?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: More details will be disclosed during  MOM's COS.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: For the IT sector, the Labour Movement has been receiving a lot of feedback from the ground, about concerns in terms of visuals and the proportion.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: And I am glad that the Minister shared that there is a two-third/one-third kind of proportion in the sector.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: But of course, there are specific companies, as what the hon Member Desmond Choo has shared, that they are "double weak"; sometimes even "triple weak".

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, I suggest that MOM take this seriously and be more rigorous as well as more resolute in measures against those companies which really demonstrate themselves to be "double weak" and are still recalcitrant.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, I agree with the Member that we ought to take this seriously.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As I have mentioned earlier, during MOM's Committee of Supply (COS), I will share more information on our action plan forward.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Minister, I filed a Parliamentary Question (PQ) sometime ago which also talks about this.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I suggested that beyond the stick approach, we should also have the carrot approach.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Perhaps, your answer may be that "this will be addressed at the COS".

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I certainly hope so, so that we consider recognising companies which are good role models  through the COS with some good announcements for them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, please wait for my reply at the COS.
